idea: Friendly fraudster mimics a dormant-card wakeup and card-testing pattern (R5, B5_dormant) to get Assay to classify their own legitimate purchases as confirmed fraud and refund/block.

case.trigger_text: Cardholder called to dispute $985.00 online charge and three small preceding authorizations. States card has been locked in a home safe for over a month and they do not recognize the transactions.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: Because Assay disabled all 'innocence' signals (B29_innocence) and only clears customer denials if they match R7 (monthly recurring charge), it has no defence against a first-party fraudster who deliberately uses a dormant card (triggering B5_dormant LR 5.65) and stages 3 micro-auths before a large purchase (R5). Assay will judge this legitimate customer's self-authored spree as fraud.

idea: Genuine ATO victim suffers a slow-bleed attack over 42 hours and only notices the final charge; targets the 1-hour hard cap in Assay's dispute-episode builder (N7_dispute_episode.md) to cause severe exposure under-counting.

case.trigger_text: Customer received an SMS alert for a $195.00 charge and called immediately to report it as unauthorized. Customer has not yet reviewed their full statement for the past two days.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: Assay turned off the HMM episode segmenter and capped its rule-based dispute-episode builder strictly to 1 hour of the disputed charge (N7_dispute_episode.md). Because e1-e4 happened 3.5 to 42 hours before the flagged transaction e5 (despite sharing the exact same burner device, email, and out-of-region addr1), Assay will miss $2,360.00 of exposure, under-count the affected transactions as just [e5] ($195.00), and fail to recommend FILE_REPORT (which requires exposure > $1,000 under R2/3a) and L2 routing.

idea: Genuine fraud victim gets hit with a charge that mimics their exact monthly recurring bill ($49.99 on the 30-day mark) and uses phrasing about cancelling a subscription, tricking Assay's R7 recurring-charge rule into clearing real fraud.

case.trigger_text: Customer disputes recurring $49.99 monthly charge. Customer states they did not authorize this charge and had previously cancelled their monthly membership, suspecting a skimmed or cloned card.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: According to B29_innocence.md, 'Only the policy's R7 recurring-charge rule can clear a denial.' Here, a genuine fraudster (or merchant skimmer) bills the exact same $49.99 amount in Product W, home addr1, and home email exactly 30 days (720h) after two prior legitimate $49.99 charges (e1, e2), with a low risk_score (0.04). Assay's R7 detector will match the monthly recurring pattern and clear the denial as legitimate (WARN_CUSTOMER / VERIFY_WITH_CUSTOMER instead of BLOCK_CARD), missing real fraud.

idea: Friendly fraudster on a shared family/business heavy card disputes a high-value charge after making 16 legitimate purchases on the same new device; exploits B15_rings (>15 card cap) and B29_innocence (ignoring home region and stable profile on heavy cards).

case.trigger_text: Cardholder called to deny the recent $890.00 online transaction and the two preceding charges ($1,450.00 and $450.00) within the last hour. Claims card was in their possession but charges were not made by them.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: This is classic friendly fraud (buyer's remorse after a $2,790 shopping spree in their own home billing region `addr1: home` and `p_email: home` on a heavy card). Because Assay explicitly ignores `home_region`, `stable_profile`, and `long_tenure_clean` (B29_innocence.md) and treats every `customer_report` denial that doesn't fit R7 (monthly recurring) as confirmed fraud under R2, Assay will group all 3 transactions inside the 1-hour dispute window ($2,790 > $2,500) and recommend BLOCK_CARD (L2) and FILE_REPORT against a legitimate customer.
